text.p: Franco-Nevada Mining Corp Ltd and its sister gold company Euro-Nevada Mining Corp Ltd surged on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday on rising gold prices and optimism over its Nevada project.
Franco-Nevada was up C$3 to C$52 and Euro-Nevada rose C$2.40 to C$36.55 in moderate morning trading.
While a stronger gold bullion price Friday could explain part of the rise, analysts said investors must also have their eyes on the companies' Midas joint venture in Nevada.
The latest news about the project was released on Tuesday, when the companies said they were increasing their exploration and drilling budget to US$12 million from US$4.5 million.

The companies do not expect to release any drill results from the property until December, when a pre-feasibility study to develop the Rex-Grande deposit would be ready, said chief financial officer Ron Binns in an interview.
But several analysts have visited the property recently, and more were expected to do so soon, he said.
"I think they like what they see," Binns said. "They may be talking up the stock."
